lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: CHAPTER 22

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Desert Remembers
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The first three days were almost ordinary.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The desert remained what it had always been: heat that baked thought into dust, wind that found every seam in clothing, and long stretches of nothing that made a man question every choice that had brought him there. The dunes looked frozen in the act of becoming waves. Wind had carved ribs into the sand where forgotten roads once ran. Zeek had crossed enough of it to know that ordinary did not mean safe. It only meant nothing had decided to kill them yet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They rode in a loose line. BAH-lahg led the donkeys, muttering the old wards his grandfather had taught him whenever the wind shifted. En-HEH-doo rode ahead, watching the horizon the way a thief watches a locked door. Ninsun kept to the middle, writing whenever they stopped. Zeek brought up the rear, the journal heavy against his ribs and the mark on his palm itching worse with every mile.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: On the second night, around a small fire, the friction that had been simmering since the gate finally surfaced.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun spread three scraps of parchment across her knees.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: We should be documenting everything. The map, the symbol, the exact location of the first chamber, the way the writing changes. This knowledge could alter how the entire region is understood.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek was checking a donkey's strap.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: We document what sells. The rest is weight.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: That is an astonishingly small way to look at the world.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: It's a practical way.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg poked the fire.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Some things should stay buried. My grandfather said the deep desert doesn't forget. It just waits for someone stupid enough to remind it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo's voice came from the shadows.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Then we remind it with a sharp knife and a heavier purse. Knowledge is a weapon. Stop treating it like a sacred relic.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked at her.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You say that like you've ever learned anything you couldn't sell.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: I've learned plenty of things I couldn't sell.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Name one.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo considered, then smiled without warmth.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg gave a short nod, as if the answer confirmed something he had already decided.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Thought so.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The silence that followed was sharper than the argument.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun shook her head.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: You are all impossible.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek said nothing. The argument was older than any of them; it had simply found new mouths.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The third day brought the first wrong thing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They found an old well just before dusk—an ancient ring of stone half-buried in sand, the remains of a road running past it toward nowhere. Footprints led to the edge and stopped. None led away.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg circled it twice before approaching.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Someone's used it recently.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: While the others examined the tracks, he crouched at the rim, took a small carved bead from a pouch at his belt, and set it carefully on the stones. No one commented. Later, when Ninsun asked why, he only said,

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Payment.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: When she asked to whom, he answered,
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Exactly.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked down the shaft. The darkness was deeper than the angle of the sun allowed. He lowered the bucket. The rope paid out far longer than the depth should have permitted. When the bucket finally struck water the sound that came back was wrong—hollow, delayed, almost like an answer.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They drank. The water was warm, yet it tasted of iron and cold stone, as though it had never seen sunlight.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: That night the donkeys refused to graze. Both animals stood rigid, ears pointed toward the same empty stretch of dark. En-HEH-doo was the first to speak.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Did anyone hear that?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: No one had. The donkeys had.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A thin line appeared in the sand several paces beyond the firelight, moving slowly toward the camp as if something beneath the surface were dragging a finger across the desert. It stopped. The mark on Zeek's palm went cold. Then the line vanished.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg got the animals under control.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: We leave at first light.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: No one disagreed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek sat apart with the journal. The page he had left blank was no longer blank. A single line had appeared in a hand that was not his father's and not quite his own:

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NOT YET.
lines.note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He closed the book before anything else could form.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Somewhere beyond the firelight the desert shifted, patient and vast, as if it had only just remembered their names.
